_comment: Gamepad stick conditioning. Matched against Input.GetJoyName() by case-insensitive substring;
the first matching profile wins, otherwise 'default' is used. Matching is by NAME because on
Quest/Android GetJoyGuid() returns the ASCII of the name and GetJoyInfo() has no vendor/product
(see devai/GAMEPAD_SUPPORT_PLAN.md, Phase 0 results).
HOW MERGING WORKS -- read before editing:
'default' is loaded first, then a matching profile overwrites EVERY field it declares.
A profile must therefore declare only what genuinely differs from default. On 2026-07-25
the Xbox profile restated all six fields, so retuning 'default' had no effect on the Xbox
pad and the sticks stayed twitchy for another flight. Keep profiles minimal.
deadzone   : stick offset ignored around centre. Measured resting offsets on the Xbox Series X
pad were up to 0.06, so anything below ~0.10 lets the drone drift on its own.
exponent   : response curve. 1.0 = linear, higher = gentler near centre while keeping full
authority at the extremes. TURN THIS FIRST when the sticks feel twitchy.
1.5 -> 2.5 cuts the command at half stick to roughly a third on every axis.
yaw/throttle/roll/pitch : per-axis sensitivity multipliers, applied after the curve. These DO
reduce full-deflection authority, so prefer 'exponent' unless one axis alone is hot.
roll/pitch  full stick = DroneControl.stick_strength m/s of target GROUND SPEED.
param-api-mixer.txt sets ANGLE_CONTROL_ENABLE 0, so these channels
feed the horizontal SPEED loop -- the earlier note here claiming the
15.0 was an angle matching PID_POS_MAX_ROLL/PITCH was wrong, and that
mistake is what hid the 45 deg 'roll and pitch get mixed' fault for a
day. stick_strength is now 3.0 m/s (reachable); these stay at 1.0.
throttle    PutVertical gets stick_vertical_strength (15.0) against the altitude
loop's PID_ALT_MAX_SPD = 5.5. 0.18 * 15 = 2.7 m/s full scale.
MEASURED GOOD in run17: commands of 0.4 / 0.9 / 1.9 / 2.5 m/s gave
climb rates of 0.40 / 0.93 / 1.91 / 2.46 m/s. Lower to ~0.13 if a
2 m/s trainer ceiling is wanted.
yaw         full stick = stick_yaw_strength (100.0) * this. run17 measures the
airframe at ~87 deg/s per unit of that command, so 0.12 meant roughly
600-1000 deg/s at full stick -- which is the whole 'it spins when I
touch the throttle' report, not stick noise. 0.014 * 100 * 87 =
~120 deg/s, the usual trainer figure. MEASURED.
yaw_deadzone / yaw_exponent : optional per-axis overrides for the YAW axis only. Omit either
one and it inherits 'deadzone' / 'exponent'. They exist because yaw has to solve a
problem the other axes do not: on the Touch stick, X leaks a median 0.34 (max
0.60) while Y is held up for throttle. run18 confirmed 0.014 with the shared
0.15 / 2.5 pair holds that leak to 1.9 deg/s -- but it also left real yaw inputs
feeling dead (~13 deg/s at half stick), which is the 'yaw feels bad' report.
The split fixes both: the deadzone absorbs the leak, the curve carries the feel.
TO RETUNE (no rebuild -- push this file, restart the app):
yaw feels dead in the middle  -> lower yaw_exponent (1.4 -> 1.0 is linear)
it spins when you throttle    -> raise yaw_deadzone (0.30 -> 0.40)
full stick too fast / slow    -> change yaw (0.014 == ~120 deg/s at full)
Startup logs the values in use: [XRInput] tuning: ... yawdz=... yawexp=...
The yaw gain is the airframe's, not the stick's, so 'default' (gamepad) needed the same
0.014. It does NOT get a yaw_deadzone: the cross-talk above is the Touch thumbstick's
geometry, and a pad's measured resting offset is only 0.04-0.06.
See devai/YAW_THROTTLE_SENSITIVITY.md.
To retune on-device WITHOUT rebuilding, push a copy of this file to:
adb push gamepad_tuning.json /sdcard/Android/data/com.hakoniwa.dronesimulator/files/
then restart the app (or power-cycle the pad). The external file overrides this one.
_comment_xr: The 'xr' section conditions the Quest Touch controllers (HakoDroneXrInputManager). It is
merged over 'default' exactly like a gamepad profile, so declare only what differs.
Until 2026-07-26 the XR path had these values hard-coded at deadzone 0.15 / exponent 1.5 and
EVERY sensitivity 1.0 -- yaw ran 8x and throttle 5.5x hotter than the gamepad, even though
both feed the same DroneControl.stick_yaw_strength (100) and stick_strength (15). That is the
whole reason the Xbox pad felt right while the Touch controllers were reported as too
The values below started as the gamepad's set, transplanted; 'yaw' is now set from run17's
measured yaw rates instead (see the yaw note above). One Touch-specific fact came out of that
flight: pushing the LEFT thumbstick fully up also deflects it sideways by 0.34 on average and
up to 0.60 (n=117 samples with the throttle past half). That is the thumb's geometry, not a
fault, and no deadzone that still leaves yaw usable can clear 0.34 -- but at yaw 0.014 the
leak is worth only ~3 deg/s, so it no longer matters. Do not raise 'yaw' back without either
re-measuring that cross-talk or giving yaw its own, much larger deadzone.

profiles._comment: Resting offsets measured at 0.04-0.06 on a Series X pad; 0.15 clears them. Everything else inherits 'default'.
Sticks recentre tighter than Xbox, so a smaller deadzone is usable. UNVERIFIED on hardware.
DS4 sticks wear and drift more, so a wider deadzone. UNVERIFIED on hardware.
